name: Polar bear
headline: length
subtitle: Adult polar bear, head and body
description: The polar bear lives on Arctic sea ice and hunts seals; along with the brown bear it is the largest land carnivore. Most adults measure about 1.8 to 2.7 m in head and body length. Males are roughly twice the weight of females, normally 350 to 590 kg against 150 to 295 kg, and the biggest bears can stand about 3 m tall on their hind legs.

measures.label: Mass (adult male)
measures.note: Adult males normally weigh 350 to 590 kg (772 to 1,300 lb)

measures.label: Mass (adult female)
measures.note: Adult females usually weigh 150 to 295 kg (331 to 650 lb), more in some regions

measures.label: Heaviest on record
measures.note: One polar bear on record weighed more than 1,700 lb (770 kg)

facts.text: Newborn cubs weigh a little over half a kilogram (about 1 lb) and are about 30 to 35 cm long, blind and toothless.
Males may measure over 3.7 m (12 ft) when standing on their hind legs, which is why most experts call polar bears the longest bears.
Pregnant females can weigh more than 453 kg (1,000 lb) before denning.
A polar bear's fat layer can be 5 to 10 cm (2 to 4 in) thick.
Polar bears can eat more than 45 kg (100 lb) of blubber in one sitting.

sources.title: Polar Bear Facts: Adaptations and Characteristics

caveats: Polar Bears International gives weights but no body length; the length comes from San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance and covers adults of both sexes.

Sources disagree on standing height: Polar Bears International says polar bears can 'stand 3 meters tall', while San Diego Zoo says males may exceed 12 ft (3.7 m) on their hind legs. The PBI figure is stored as the measure.
San Diego Zoo gives male weights of 300 to 635 kg for most males, a wider range than PBI's 350 to 590 kg; the PBI range is stored.
The Alaska Department of Fish and Game page returned no content, and USFWS was not used.
